units.locator: Article 32. Evaluation of procurement participants' applications and criteria for that evaluation
units.text: 10) derivative works;
units.label: Point 10 Part 7 Art. 32

units.locator: Article 32. Evaluation of procurement participants' applications and criteria for that evaluation
units.text: 11) composite works, other than databases, whose selection or arrangement of materials constitutes creative work.
units.label: Point 11 Part 7 Art. 32

units.locator: Article 32. Evaluation of procurement participants' applications and criteria for that evaluation
units.text: 8. The Government of the Russian Federation shall establish the procedure for evaluating applications, including limits on the weight of each criterion. Where regulated prices (tariffs) for goods, works or services have been established under legislation of the Russian Federation, the contracting authority may omit the criteria specified in points 1 and 2 of part 1 of this Article when evaluating applications.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 32

units.locator: Article 32. Evaluation of procurement participants' applications and criteria for that evaluation
units.text: 9. A contracting authority may not use criteria not provided for by this Article or weights other than those established by part 6 of this Article and under part 8 of this Article. If the contracting authority fails to meet this requirement, the selection of a supplier (contractor, service provider) may be declared invalid on a claim brought by one or more procurement participants.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 32

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.label: Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 1. In the cases provided for by this Federal Law, the contracting authority must observe the following rules when describing the procurement subject matter:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 1) the description shall specify the functional, technical and quality characteristics and, where necessary, operational characteristics of the procurement subject matter. It must not include requirements or references relating to trademarks, service marks, business names, patents, utility models, industrial designs or the name of the country of origin, or requirements for goods, information, works or services, if such requirements or references restrict the number of procurement participants. A trademark may be referred to in the description in the following cases:
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: а) the reference is accompanied by the words “or equivalent”;
units.label: Subpoint «а» Point 1 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: б) goods bearing other trademarks are incompatible and compatibility with goods used by the contracting authority must be ensured;
units.label: Subpoint «б» Point 1 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: в) spare parts and consumables for machines and equipment used by the contracting authority are procured in accordance with their technical documentation;
units.label: Subpoint «в» Point 1 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: г) medical devices or specialized therapeutic nutrition products are procured because they must be prescribed to a patient on medical grounds, namely individual intolerance or vital indications, by decision of a medical commission recorded in the patient’s medical documentation and the commission’s register. The Government of the Russian Federation shall approve the list of those devices and products and the procedure for drawing it up;
units.label: Subpoint «г» Point 1 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 2) the description shall use indicators, requirements, symbols and terminology concerning technical and functional characteristics (consumer properties) of goods, works or services and quality characteristics of the procurement subject matter provided for by technical regulations adopted under technical regulation legislation of the Russian Federation and documents developed and used in the national standardization system adopted under standardization legislation of the Russian Federation, as well as other requirements concerning determination of whether the goods supplied, works performed or services provided meet the contracting authority’s needs. If the contracting authority does not use the indicators, requirements, symbols and terminology established under technical regulation and standardization legislation, the description must justify the need to use other ones;
units.label: Point 2 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 3) the description may include specifications, plans, drawings, sketches, photographs, results of work or testing, and requirements, including those concerning tests, testing methods, packaging under the Civil Code of the Russian Federation, marking, labels, conformity assessment, production processes and methods under technical regulations, documents developed and used in the national standardization system and technical specifications, and concerning symbols and terminology;
units.label: Point 3 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 4) if the description requires the goods supplied to conform to an image of the goods covered by the contract, it must contain an image enabling the goods to be identified and an application to be prepared;
units.label: Point 4 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 5) if the description requires the goods supplied to conform to a sample or model of the goods covered by the contract, it must state the location, opening and closing dates, procedure and schedule for participants to inspect that sample or model;
units.label: Point 5 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 6) where medicinal products are being procured, the description must state their international non-proprietary names or, where those do not exist, their chemical or group names. The contracting authority may specify trade names when procuring medicines on the list of medicines procured by trade name, and when procuring medicines necessary for a patient throughout treatment on medical grounds, namely individual intolerance or vital indications, by decision of a medical commission recorded in the patient’s medical documentation and the register of decisions adopted at commission meetings, through an electronic request for quotations under subpoint “г” of point 2 of part 10 of Article 24 of this Federal Law or through closed competitive methods. The Government of the Russian Federation shall approve that list and the procedure for drawing it up. Where medicinal products are procured, a single contract (lot) may not include medicines with different international non-proprietary names or, where those do not exist, different chemical or group names, if the initial (maximum) contract price (lot price) exceeds the threshold set by the Government of the Russian Federation; nor may a single contract (lot) combine medicines specified by international non-proprietary names, or chemical or group names where those do not exist, with medicines specified by trade names. This point shall not apply when selecting a supplier of medicines with whom a contract with reciprocal investment obligations is concluded under Article 111.4 of this Federal Law;
units.label: Point 6 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 7) Unless the description provides otherwise, the goods supplied must be new, meaning goods that have not been used, repaired or refurbished, whose components have not been replaced and whose consumer properties have not been restored;
units.label: Point 7 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 8) for procurement of construction, reconstruction, major repair or demolition works on a capital construction project, the description must include design documentation approved under urban development legislation, standard design documentation or a cost estimate for major repairs, except where that legislation does not require preparation of such documentation or an estimate, and except procurement under parts 16 and 16.1 of Article 34 of this Federal Law where the contract subject matter includes design of the capital construction project. Inclusion of design documentation under this point constitutes proper compliance with points 1–3 of this part and part 2 of this Article.
units.label: Point 8 Part 1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 1.1. When describing goods being procured, including goods supplied in performing the procured works or providing the procured services, that are subject to a prohibition, restriction or preference provided for by point 1 of part 2 of Article 14 of this Federal Law, characteristics of goods of Russian origin shall be specified, except in cases established by the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1.1 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 2. A description prepared under part 1 of this Article must contain indicators enabling the procured goods, works or services to be assessed against the contracting authority’s requirements. Maximum and/or minimum values and/or values that may not be changed shall be specified.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 3. The description must not include, including in the form of quality or technical requirements for goods, works or services or functional requirements (consumer properties) for goods, requirements concerning the manufacturer or procurement participant, including qualifications and work experience, or the participant’s business reputation, production capacity, technological equipment, workforce, financial or other resources needed to produce the goods or perform the works or services covered by the contract, except where this Federal Law permits such requirements for a participant.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 4. Where necessary, the contracting authority shall establish requirements for quality guarantees for goods, works or services, the warranty period and/or scope of those guarantees, warranty servicing of goods (hereinafter, warranty obligations), operating costs, mandatory installation and commissioning, and training of persons who will use and service the goods. When selecting a supplier of machines or equipment, the contracting authority shall set requirements for the warranty period and/or scope of quality guarantees, warranty servicing and servicing costs during the warranty period, and installation and commissioning where required by the goods’ technical documentation. When selecting a supplier of new machines or equipment, the contracting authority shall require a manufacturer’s and/or supplier’s guarantee and specify its duration. The guarantee shall be provided together with the goods.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 5. The Government of the Russian Federation may establish special rules for describing certain types of procurement subject matter.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 33

units.locator: Article 33. Rules for describing the procurement subject matter
units.text: 6. Special rules for describing procurement subject matter under the state defence order may be established by Federal Law of 29 December 2012 No. 275-FZ “On the State Defence Order”.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 33

units.text: Article 34. Contract
units.label: Art. 34

units.text: 1. A contract shall be concluded on the terms set out in the procurement notice or invitation, procurement documentation and the application of the participant with whom it is concluded, except where this Federal Law does not provide for the notice or invitation, documentation or application. In the case provided for by part 24 of Article 22 of this Federal Law, the contract must contain the procedure for determining the quantity of goods or volume of works or services and the delivery or performance time limit or limits on the basis of the contracting authority’s orders.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 34

units.text: 2. On conclusion, a contract shall state that its price is fixed for its entire performance period. In the case provided for by part 24 of Article 22 of this Federal Law, it shall state unit prices of goods, works or services and the maximum contract price. In cases established by the Government of the Russian Federation, it shall state the indicative price or price formula and maximum price specified by the contracting authority in the procurement notice and procurement documentation, where such documentation is provided for by this Federal Law. Essential contract terms may not be changed on conclusion or during performance, except in cases provided for by this Federal Law. If the draft contract provides for separate performance stages, each stage’s price shall be reduced in proportion to the reduction in the initial (maximum) contract price offered by the participant with whom the contract is concluded.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 34

units.text: 3. Special rules for determining the price of a state contract for goods, works or services under the state defence order, taking account of part 2 of this Article, may be established by Federal Law of 29 December 2012 No. 275-FZ “On the State Defence Order”.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 34

units.text: 4. The contract shall include a mandatory clause on liability of the contracting authority and supplier (contractor, service provider) for failure to perform or improper performance of contractual obligations.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 34

units.text: 5. If the contracting authority delays performance of contractual obligations or otherwise fails to perform or improperly performs them, the supplier (contractor, service provider) may demand contractual penalties (fines and delay penalties). A delay penalty shall accrue for each day of delay, starting on the day after the contractual deadline. The contract shall set it at one three-hundredth of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation’s key rate in effect on the payment date, applied to the amount not paid on time. Fines shall be charged for improper performance other than delay. The contract shall set the fine in the manner established by the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 34

units.text: 6. If the supplier (contractor, service provider) delays performance of contractual obligations, including warranty obligations, or otherwise fails to perform or improperly performs them, the contracting authority shall demand payment of contractual penalties (fines and late-performance penalties).
units.label: Part 6 Art. 34

units.text: 6.1. Repealed from 1 January 2017. — Federal Law of 29.12.2015 No. 390-FZ.
units.label: Part 6.1 Art. 34

units.text: 7. A penalty shall accrue for each day of delay by the supplier (contractor, service provider), starting on the day after the contractual deadline. The contract shall set it at one three-hundredth of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation’s key rate in effect on the payment date, applied to the contract price or price of the separate performance stage, reduced by an amount proportional to the obligations under the contract or relevant stage actually performed by the supplier (contractor, service provider), unless legislation of the Russian Federation establishes a different calculation procedure.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 34

units.text: 8. Fines shall be charged for the supplier’s (contractor’s, service provider’s) failure to perform or improper performance of contractual obligations, other than delay, including delay in warranty obligations. The contract shall set the fine in the manner established by the Government of the Russian Federation unless legislation of the Russian Federation establishes a different calculation procedure.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 34

units.text: 9. A party shall be exempt from contractual penalties (fines or late-performance penalties) if it proves that failure to perform or improper performance resulted from force majeure or the fault of the other party.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 34

units.text: 9.1. The Government of the Russian Federation may establish cases and a procedure for writing off contractual penalties (fines and late-performance penalties) accrued against a supplier (contractor, service provider) for failure to perform or improper performance but not written off by the contracting authority.
units.label: Part 9.1 Art. 34

units.text: 10. In tenders, contracts may be concluded with several participants for the supply of technical rehabilitation aids for persons with disabilities; creation of several literary or artistic works; research, including two or more research works forming a single contract subject matter on the same subject and with identical contract terms; educational, sanatorium treatment and health improvement services; services for children’s recreation and health improvement, including vouchers; works (services) for creation, development, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of information systems; or supply of software and hardware and information and communications equipment. The contracting authority shall specify the right to conclude contracts with several participants in the procurement notice and procurement documentation, where such documentation is provided for by this Federal Law. When procuring two or more research works on the same subject and with identical contract terms, the initial (maximum) price specified shall be that of one contract; all such contracts shall have the same initial (maximum) price, and the initial (maximum) lot price shall equal the total of those prices.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 34

units.text: 11. The Government of the Russian Federation may establish standard contract terms to be applied by contracting authorities in procurement.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 34

units.text: 12. A contract concluded for more than three years and priced at more than one hundred million rubles must include a contract performance schedule.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 34

units.text: 13. The contract shall include mandatory terms:
units.label: Part 13 Art. 34

units.text: 1) on the procedure and time limits for payment for goods, works or services, taking account of part 13 of Article 37 of this Federal Law; the procedure and time limits for acceptance by the contracting authority of goods supplied, works performed (their results) or services provided, as regards their quantity, completeness and volume meeting the contract requirements; the procedure and time limits for recording acceptance results; and the procedure and deadline for the supplier (contractor, service provider) to provide security for warranty obligations where required under Article 96 of this Federal Law. In the case provided for by part 24 of Article 22 of this Federal Law, the contract must state that payment is made at the unit price on the basis of the quantity of goods supplied or volume of works or services actually performed, but may not exceed the maximum contract price. Where the contract provides for staged performance and an advance payment, it shall specify the advance for each stage as a percentage of that stage’s price;
units.label: Point 1 Part 13 Art. 34

units.text: 2) on reducing the amount payable by the contracting authority to a legal entity or individual, including an individual entrepreneur, by taxes, levies and other mandatory payments to budgets within the budget system of the Russian Federation connected with payment under the contract, where tax and levy legislation requires the contracting authority to pay those amounts to the budgets.
units.label: Point 2 Part 13 Art. 34

units.text: 13.1. Where a contract is concluded following supplier (contractor, service provider) selection for which the notice was published in the unified information system or invitations were sent from 1 January through 30 April 2022 inclusive, the contractual period for the contracting authority to pay for goods supplied, works performed (their results), services provided or separate performance stages must not exceed fifteen working days, and from 1 May 2022 it must not exceed seven working days. In both cases the period runs from the date on which the contracting authority signs the acceptance document provided for by part 7 of Article 94 of this Federal Law, except where:
units.label: Part 13.1 Art. 34

units.text: 1) legislation of the Russian Federation establishes a different payment period;
units.label: Point 1 Part 13.1 Art. 34

units.text: 2) the acceptance document is drawn up without using the unified information system; payment must then be made within ten working days of signature of the acceptance document under part 7 of Article 94 of this Federal Law, or within twenty working days if the contract contains a state secret;
units.label: Point 2 Part 13.1 Art. 34

units.text: 3) payments under the contract, or advance payments under it, are subject to treasury support under legislation of the Russian Federation; payment must then be made within ten working days of signature of the acceptance document under part 7 of Article 94 of this Federal Law;
units.label: Point 3 Part 13.1 Art. 34

units.text: 4) the Government of the Russian Federation has established another payment period to ensure defence capability and state security.
units.label: Point 4 Part 13.1 Art. 34

units.text: 14. The contract may include terms:
units.label: Part 14 Art. 34

units.text: 1) permitting unilateral refusal to perform the contract under parts 8–11, 13–19, 21–23 and 25 of Article 95 of this Federal Law;
units.label: Point 1 Part 14 Art. 34

units.text: 2) permitting deduction, from the amount payable to the supplier (contractor, service provider), of unpaid contractual penalties (fines and late-performance penalties) demanded by the contracting authority under this Federal Law.
units.label: Point 2 Part 14 Art. 34

units.text: 15. When concluding a contract in the cases provided for by point 1, points 4 and 5 except contracts under part 12 of Article 93 of this Federal Law, and points 8, 9, 15, 20, 21, 22, 23, 26, 28, 29, 33, 37, 40, 41, 44, 45, 46, 50–53, 56 and 63 of part 1 of Article 93 of this Federal Law, the contracting authority may omit the requirements of parts 4–9 and 11–13 of this Article. In those cases, the contract may be concluded in simple written form under the transaction provisions of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 15 Art. 34

units.text: 16. The contracting authority may conclude a life-cycle contract for new machines and equipment and in other cases established by the Government of the Russian Federation. The contract must state the life-cycle cost of the goods or facility created through works, comprising:
units.label: Part 16 Art. 34

units.text: 1) the cost of goods or works, including, where necessary, the costs of preparing design documentation and creating the goods;
units.label: Point 1 Part 16 Art. 34

units.text: 2) the cost of subsequent servicing, operation during the service life where necessary, repair and/or disposal of the goods supplied or the capital construction project or goods created through works.
units.label: Point 2 Part 16 Art. 34

units.text: 16.1. A contract may simultaneously cover design, construction and commissioning of capital construction projects. The Government of the Russian Federation shall establish the procedure and grounds for concluding such contracts.
units.label: Part 16.1 Art. 34

units.text: 16.2. A contract may simultaneously cover conservation, repair, restoration and adaptation for modern use of a cultural heritage site (historical and cultural monument) of the peoples of the Russian Federation, including research, surveys, design and production works, scientific direction of preservation works, and technical and designer supervision of those works.
units.label: Part 16.2 Art. 34

units.text: 16.3. Where standard design documentation is included in the description under point 8 of part 1 of Article 33 of this Federal Law, the contract may simultaneously cover preparation of design documentation and/or engineering surveys and construction works on a capital construction project.
units.label: Part 16.3 Art. 34

units.text: 17. Where the Government of the Russian Federation has established additional performance conditions for a particular procurement under part 1 of Article 111 of this Federal Law, including conditions unrelated to the contract subject matter, those conditions shall be included in the contract.
units.label: Part 17 Art. 34

units.text: 18. Repealed from 1 January 2022. — Federal Law of 02.07.2021 No. 360-FZ.
units.label: Part 18 Art. 34

units.text: 19 - 21. Repealed from 1 January 2014. — Federal Law of 28.12.2013 No. 396-FZ.
units.label: Part 18 Art. 34 · “19 - 21. Repealed from 1 January 2014. — Federal Law of…”

units.text: 22. A court may declare a contract invalid, including at the request of a procurement control body, if personal interest of the contracting authority’s head, a procurement commission member, head of its contract service or contract manager in its conclusion or performance is established. Such interest consists of the possibility for those officials to obtain income in the form of money, valuables, other property, including property rights, property-related services, or other benefits for themselves or third parties.
units.label: Part 22 Art. 34

units.text: 23. Where the initial (maximum) contract price exceeds the amount set by the Government of the Russian Federation, the contract must require the supplier (contractor, service provider) to provide information on all co-performers and subcontractors with which it concludes an agreement or agreements whose price or combined price exceeds ten percent of the contract price.
units.label: Part 23 Art. 34

units.text: 24. The supplier (contractor, service provider) shall provide the information specified in part 23 of this Article within ten days of concluding the agreement with the co-performer or subcontractor. The contract must provide liability for failure to supply it, by recovery of a daily penalty from the supplier (contractor, service provider) equal to one three-hundredth of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation’s key rate in effect on the payment date, applied to the price of the agreement concluded with the co-performer or subcontractor under this part. The penalty shall accrue for each day of delay in fulfilling that obligation.
units.label: Part 24 Art. 34

units.text: 25. If the supplier (contractor, service provider) fails to provide the information specified in part 23 of this Article, that failure shall be recorded in the unified information system. Failure to provide the information does not, on that ground alone, render the concluded contract invalid.
units.label: Part 25 Art. 34
